fields_note.opening_hours_fixture: Weekday schedule mon-sun in local time. Null whole field = no confirmed exercise opening window. Null weekday = closed in exercise. End earlier than start (e.g. 20:00-02:00) means next calendar day. 00:00-24:00 = continuous access in this *exercise only*.

pois.name: Old Fortress
pois.description: The Old Fortress occupies the rocky promontory east of Corfu's Old Town and forms part of the town's UNESCO-listed defensive ensemble. Venetian engineers developed bastions, ramparts and two high points separated from the town by a sea moat; later British-period buildings remain visible within the walls. An entrance bridge leads through the western fortifications, while uphill passages open views towards the town and the sea. It is an extensive, partly exposed visit rather than a single viewpoint, so a walking plan should reserve time for elevation changes.

pois.name: New Fortress
pois.description: The New Fortress overlooks the old harbour from the western side of Corfu's historic centre. Its Venetian defensive works include substantial stone bastions, passages and multiple levels; later British structures form part of the complex. The upper areas offer views of rooftops and the harbour, but reaching them takes more time than viewing the entrance gate alone. In a short itinerary, its earlier closing fixture and the uphill approach should be considered before inserting it late in the afternoon.
pois.description_provenance: Curated from supplied POI export and linked background references

pois.name: Kremasti Square and Cistern
pois.description: Kremasti Square lies among the closely spaced lanes of Campiello, a neighbourhood shaped by Corfu's Venetian period. Its ornamented stone cistern records the central place of shared water storage in the life of the Old Town. The small square provides a short architecture and local-history stop rather than a large indoor attraction. It pairs naturally with nearby churches and residential streets, but its open-air character makes it a less suitable rain substitute.

pois.name: Saint Spyridon Church
pois.description: The Church of Saint Spyridon is dedicated to Corfu's patron saint and is one of the island's most important religious sites. The present church dates from the late sixteenth century; its tall bell tower recalls that of San Giorgio dei Greci in Venice. Inside are post-Byzantine artworks and a silver reliquary associated with Saint Spyridon's relics. The presence of a place of worship does not establish visitor access at any particular hour: indoor access must remain unconfirmed if no schedule is supplied.

pois.name: Campiello Quarter
pois.description: Campiello is one of the oldest quarters of Corfu's Old Town, with tight lanes, stairways, small squares and buildings showing the influence of centuries of Venetian rule. The district's layout resembles the small urban campielli found in Venice, while churches and former noble houses add layers of local history. It is best experienced as a slow outdoor walk rather than a fixed-duration museum visit. A sensible route can connect Campiello with Kremasti Square and Saint Spyridon Church without excessive backtracking.

pois.name: Maitland Rotunda
pois.description: The circular Maitland Rotunda stands in the southern section of Spianada Square. Built in 1816 to honour the British commissioner Thomas Maitland, it marks a transition from the island's Venetian defences to its British-period civic architecture. The neoclassical structure also occupies a place associated with a former public cistern, connecting the site's appearance to the square's earlier practical role. It is a brief exterior stop and can be combined with a Spianada walk or nearby monuments.

pois.name: Casa Parlante Museum
pois.description: Casa Parlante recreates daily life in a nineteenth-century Corfiot noble household within a historic Old Town mansion. Period-style rooms, furnishings, animated figures, sounds and other sensory details are used to explain domestic routines and social customs. The experience differs from a conventional gallery of static objects, offering a focused introduction to local social history. It is an indoor candidate for a weather-adjusted itinerary, subject to the exercise's opening-hours fixture.

pois.name: Gate of the New Fortress
pois.description: The Gate of the New Fortress forms part of the Venetian fortifications above Corfu's old harbour. Decorative stonework and the monumental approach illustrate how the town controlled movement between its port and defensive perimeter. A visit to the gate can be treated as a short exterior architecture stop; it should not be conflated with a full walk through the upper bastions of the New Fortress. The separate POI entries let an itinerary choose one or both stops without treating them as identical.

pois.name: Old Town Hall (Loggia dei Nobili)
pois.description: The former Loggia dei Nobili served as a civic gathering place before conversion into the San Giacomo theatre and later Corfu's town hall. Its Renaissance-influenced facade and location beside Town Hall Square reflect how public buildings changed use across Venetian and later periods. The building helps explain the island's longstanding musical and theatrical culture: San Giacomo was among the region's early opera venues. In this dataset the attraction is an exterior visit, not a ticketed interior tour.

pois.name: Palace of St. Michael and St. George
pois.description: The Palace of Saint Michael and Saint George was constructed under British administration in the early nineteenth century to serve official and ceremonial functions. Its grand neoclassical facade frames the northern end of Spianada and features a row of Doric columns and prominent arches. The building also housed institutions of the Ionian State and today contains the Museum of Asian Art. This POI represents the palace exterior; the museum is modelled separately so the planner can avoid counting a facade stop as an indoor museum visit.

pois.name: Corfu Philharmonic Music Museum
pois.description: The Corfu Philharmonic Society's Nikolaos Halikiopoulos Mantzaros Music Museum documents the island's distinctive band and music-education tradition. Founded in 1840, the society is among Greece's earliest institutions for organized music education; its museum opened in 2010. Displays include historic instruments, scores, photographs, documents and material linked to composer Nikolaos Mantzaros. It provides a compact indoor choice for someone interested in Corfiot cultural life rather than conventional archaeology.

pois.name: Historic Jewish Synagogue
pois.description: Corfu's surviving historic synagogue recalls a Jewish community with Romaniote and later Italian-speaking traditions. The Jewish Museum of Greece documents the community's long presence, its distinct congregations and the destruction and deportations it suffered during the Holocaust. The synagogue is a religious and historical site, not an attraction whose interior can automatically be assumed open to tourists. In a proposed itinerary, visitors may be directed to the surrounding quarter while interior access remains subject to confirmation.

pois.name: Patounis' Soap Factory
pois.description: Patounis' Soap Factory is an operating traditional olive-soap workshop established in Corfu in 1891 as part of a family enterprise whose history began earlier on Zakynthos. Original equipment and a cauldron-based soap-making process preserve an example of local industrial and craft heritage. The workshop has been recognized as an industrial-heritage monument, while its inherited soap-making technique has been recorded in Greece's inventory of intangible heritage. pois.description: The Gate of the Old Fortress lies between the Martinengo and Savorgnan bastions, at the entrance to the fortified promontory. It was historically approached across a moat; a later bridge replaced the earlier drawbridge, while the monumental entrance preserves traces of its defensive function. pois.name: Ionian Academy (Grimani Barracks)
pois.description: The Ionian Academy building began as Venetian-period military barracks, known as the Grimani Barracks, beside the southern part of Spianada. It later housed the Ionian Academy, established in 1824 and remembered as an early university of the modern Greek world. The building was badly damaged during the Second World War and subsequently restored; it is associated today with the Ionian University. pois.name: Byzantine Museum (Antivouniotissa)
pois.description: The Byzantine Museum is housed in the church of Panagia Antivouniotissa, an important example of Corfu's late medieval and post-Byzantine ecclesiastical architecture. Its collection includes portable icons from the fifteenth to nineteenth centuries and shows the importance of the island for Greek religious painting, including artists linked with the Cretan school. pois.name: Jewish Holocaust Memorial
pois.description: The Jewish Holocaust Memorial commemorates members of Corfu's Jewish community persecuted and deported during the German occupation in 1944. The Jewish Museum of Greece records the island's centuries-old Romaniote and other Jewish traditions and the destruction suffered by the community during the Second World War. Its most distinctive exhibit is the large Gorgon pediment from the Temple of Artemis, excavated in the area of ancient Palaiopolis. The collection also includes sculpture, pottery, coins and objects illustrating different periods of ancient Corfu. Today it links the Old Town's architecture, promenades, monuments and access toward the fortress.
